# Part III — Configuring the engine

One chapter for each job the ECU does. Each follows the same shape: what it does, how it works, before you start, setting it up, worked examples, tuning it, diagnostics, troubleshooting and the full settings reference.

- **[Engine and vehicle basics](engine-basics.md)** — Before rusEFI can fuel or fire anything it must know how many cylinders the engine has, how big it is, in which order the cylinders fire and whether it is a two- or four-stroke — and these few settings feed every calculation that follows.
- **[The trigger system](trigger.md)** — The trigger system reads the crank (and cam) sensors, works out exactly where the engine is in its cycle and how fast it turns, and gives every injection and spark event its angle.
- **[Sensors and calibration](sensors.md)** — Every sensor is turned into a physical unit by a calibration you supply — three resistance points for a temperature sensor, two voltage points for a pressure sensor, a tooth count for a speed sensor — and none of it means anything unless the ECU is running on 12 V with the ignition on while you set it up.
- **[Outputs and pins](outputs.md)** — An output is a job the ECU has to do — run the fuel pump, switch the cooling fan, blink the check engine lamp — and every job names one connector pin that the ECU switches; the firmware gives each pin exactly one owner and stops the engine rather than let two jobs fight over it.
- **[Fuel](fuel.md)** — RusEFI works out how much air each cylinder breathed, turns that into a mass of fuel using the target air-fuel ratio, multiplies in the corrections, then converts the mass into the milliseconds each injector is held open — and switches injection off when something needs protecting.
- **[Ignition](ignition.md)** — The ignition system charges each coil for a set time, the **dwell**, and fires it at the crank angle given by the timing table and its corrections. This chapter sets up the hardware, mode, outputs, dwell and base timing.
- **[Cranking](cranking.md)** — While the starter turns the engine, rusEFI uses a separate, simpler set of fuel, spark and idle-air settings, then hands over to the running tables with extra fuel that fades out as the engine settles.
- **[Idle](idle.md)** — The idle controller decides how much air the engine gets when the throttle is closed — a coolant-dependent opening plus a PID that trims it to hold the target RPM — and can add a small amount of ignition advance or retard to react faster than airflow alone.
- **[Electronic throttle](electronic-throttle.md)** — The electronic throttle controller reads the accelerator pedal, decides how far the throttle should be open, and drives the throttle motor until two position sensors agree that it is there — and lets go of the throttle the moment anything looks wrong.
- **[Closed-loop lambda](closed-loop-lambda.md)** — The ECU reads lambda in the exhaust, compares it with the target from the lambda table, and nudges the fuel up or down until the two agree — holding a short-term correction while it drives, and learning a long-term correction it keeps between starts.
- **[Boost](boost.md)** — Boost control drives the wastegate — through a PWM solenoid or an electronic wastegate motor — so the turbo makes the boost pressure you ask for, and the ECU cuts fuel if the pressure ever goes past a hard limit.
- **[Cam and valve control](vvt.md)** — RusEFI reads where a camshaft actually is, compares that with where a table says it should be, and trims the phaser's solenoid until the two agree — and lets go of the solenoid whenever it cannot see the cam.
- **[Launch, shift and traction](launch-traction.md)** — All three of these take drive torque away from the wheels for a moment — launch control holds the engine at a set speed while you pull away, flat shift takes torque out for the instant of an upshift, traction control reacts when the wheels start to slide — and rusEFI does it with ignition timing, ignition skipping and the throttle, never with the brakes.
- **[Limits and engine protection](limits-protection.md)** — The protection manager watches engine speed, boost, oil pressure, lambda and injector duty, and cuts fuel, spark or both the moment one of them goes outside the limits you set.
- **[Knock](knock.md)** — RusEFI listens to the knock sensor for a short window after every spark, and when the sound is louder than a threshold it takes ignition timing away, then gives it back slowly.
- **[CAN configuration](can.md)** — CAN is the two-wire network the ECU uses to talk to a dash, a wideband controller, an EGT gauge, the car's own instrument cluster and extra input/output boxes — one dialog turns the network on, a handful more decide what the ECU listens for and what it sends.
